Professor '''David Pegg''' (born 1941)<ref name=eoas>{{cite web |url=http://www.eoas.info/biogs/P003858b.htm |title=Pegg, David Thomas (1941 - ) |author=Rosanne Walker |accessdate=14 May 2012}}</ref> is an emeritus professor in theoretical [[physics]] at [[Griffith University]], [[Australia]]. In his career, he has made numerous contributions to [[NMR]], [[quantum optics]] and conceptual physics including the nature of [[time]]. He has published approximately 200 papers and has at least 12300 citations.  He is a [[list of Fellows of the Australian Academy of Science|fellow of the Australian Academy of Science]] and a Corresponding Fellow of the [[Royal Society of Edinburgh]].  He is a recipient of the [[Harrie Massey]] Medal for Australian physics<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.aip.org.au/content/massey |title=Australian Institute of Physics |access-date=13 October 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080819202912/http://www.aip.org.au/content/massey |archive-date=19 August 2008 |url-status=dead }}</ref> and of the [[Centenary Medal]]<ref>{{Cite web|title=Professor David Thomas Pegg|url=https://honours.pmc.gov.au/honours/awards/1126604|url-status=live|access-date=2021-10-27|website=It's an Honour|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211027051924/https://honours.pmc.gov.au/honours/awards/1126604 |archive-date=27 October 2021 }}</ref> for his contribution to quantum theory.  He is best known for the Pegg-Barnett phase formalism that provides a quantum mechanical description of the phase of light,<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Pegg | first1=D. T. | last2=Barnett | first2=S. M. | title=Phase properties of the quantized single-mode electromagnetic field | journal=Physical Review A | publisher=American Physical Society (APS) | volume=39 | issue=4 | date=1 January 1989 | issn=0556-2791 | doi=10.1103/physreva.39.1665 | pages=1665–1675| pmid=9901420 | bibcode=1989PhRvA..39.1665P }}</ref> for the invention of the DEPT sequence for [[nuclear magnetic resonance]]<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Pegg | first1=David T. | last2=Doddrell | first2=David M. | last3=Bendall | first3=M. Robin | title=Proton-polarization transfer enhancement of a heteronuclear spin multiplet with preservation of phase coherency and relative component intensities | journal=The Journal of Chemical Physics | publisher=AIP Publishing | volume=77 | issue=6 | date=15 September 1982 | issn=0021-9606 | doi=10.1063/1.444188 | pages=2745–2752| bibcode=1982JChPh..77.2745P }}</ref> and for the invention of the quantum scissors device.<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Pegg | first1=David T. | last2=Phillips | first2=Lee S. | last3=Barnett | first3=Stephen M. | title=Optical State Truncation by Projection Synthesis | journal=Physical Review Letters | publisher=American Physical Society (APS) | volume=81 | issue=8 | date=24 August 1998 | issn=0031-9007 | doi=10.1103/physrevlett.81.1604 | pages=1604–1606| bibcode=1998PhRvL..81.1604P }}</ref>
